title: Tony Romo Faces Three New Citations From July Wisconsin OWI Arrest
dek: CBS Sports broadcaster Tony Romo faces three citations from his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin: operating while intoxicated (first offense), unsafe passing on the right side, and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle. Romo remains indefinitely suspended from CBS's No. 1 booth, where J.J. Watt has taken his place.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Romo was cited for first-offense OWI, unsafe passing, and open intoxicants following a July 23 Wisconsin arrest where he failed a field sobriety test.
bottom_line: Romo's three citations compound the legal and professional jeopardy surrounding his indefinite suspension. Watch for the specific date of his court appearance, any formal statement from CBS on contract options or reinstatement conditions, and whether the morality clause becomes a contested legal matter between Romo and the network.
body:
Tony Romo faces three citations stemming from his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin, per Awful Announcing. The charges are operating while intoxicated (first offense), unsafe passing on the right side, and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle. Romo was pulled over and arrested after failing a field sobriety test, with an open bottle of alcohol in his car at the time.
Body camera footage from the incident was widely circulated. Romo remains indefinitely suspended from his role alongside Jim Nantz in CBS's No. 1 booth. J.J. Watt has stepped into Romo's spot during the suspension.
Romo's long-term future at CBS remains uncertain. CBS holds a 10-year, $180 million contract with Romo signed in 2020.  Awful Announcing reports that .
Awful Announcing reports that Romo's performance in the booth has taken a notable downward turn in recent years and that fan and critical sentiment has largely turned against him. By contrast, J.J. Watt and several other recent players-turned-commentators have risen to the level Romo once held among NFL audiences.
A Romo spokesperson said, per Awful Announcing: "Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."
